title: War-Damaged Six-Story Building Collapses Overnight in Gaza City's Tal al-Hawa Area, Killing at Least 20
detail: A six-story residential building known as the Al Saada building, sheltering nearly 100 people including displaced families in the Tal al-Hawa area of western Gaza City, collapsed overnight into Wednesday, September 16, 2026. Palestinian Civil Defence initially said at least 20 people were killed, including several children, and 14 more were injured; dozens remained missing under the rubble as rescue teams worked with basic hand tools, lacking heavy equipment. Civil Defence spokesperson Mahmoud Basal said the building had previously sustained structural damage from Israeli strikes earlier in the war, leaving it cracked and unstable before it gave way. Gaza's Government Media Office said the building had been 'directly targeted during the genocidal war' and blamed 'the Israeli occupation and the international community' for the collapse; the IDF did not immediately respond. Officials estimate roughly 2,000 war-damaged buildings across Gaza remain at risk of collapse, with residents returning to unsafe structures because of a severe shortage of alternative housing. UPDATE (Sep 18): an Associated Press wire report revised the confirmed death toll to 21 killed as rescue and recovery work continued; see the September 18, 2026 event for the AP report and a second, unrelated building collapse in Gaza City that day.

media.caption: Rescue teams search the rubble of the collapsed Al Saada building in the Tal al-Hawa area of Gaza City, September 16, 2026

confidenceReason: Collapse, death toll and location corroborated by Al Jazeera and Times of Israel reporting citing Palestinian Civil Defence (Tier 1), with the toll subsequently confirmed at 21 killed by an AP wire report on Sep 18.
